subject.title: feat: add readiness conditions and providers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.readiness`, the canonical readiness condition model, and `registerReadinessCriterion` as permanent core and public Plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and proven, but automated review cannot decide permanent configuration identity, fail-closed serving policy, or a new external plugin capability contract while the related RFC remains open.

options.title: Sponsor the full contract
options.body: Approve the canonical condition model and plugin criterion API, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed exact-head compatibility proof before merge.

options.title: Land a core-only slice
options.body: Keep canonical built-in conditions and the CLI projection but defer operator selectors and the public plugin registration API to a later approved contract.

options.title: Pause for the RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open without further rebases until the related readiness RFC settles the permanent API and policy shape.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the full contract
recommendation.body: Approve the canonical condition model and plugin criterion API, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed exact-head compatibility proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway policy, configuration, and public plugin contracts, matching the broadest relevant current-main history and ownership evidence.
